new_label: Warm storybook (watercolor wash, 12 fps line boil)
old_blurb: Soft watercolor washes, warm cream paper, and gentle 12fps hand-drawn line wobble — feels human, approachable, and poetic.
new_blurb: Soft watercolor on cream paper; lines wobble gently, like a hand-drawn picture book.
why: 19-word blurb; "12fps" unexplained; jargon now parenthetical in label.

new_label: Bold cut-paper poster (Saul Bass, 3 colors, 8 fps snaps)
old_blurb: Sharp scissors-cut paper shapes, 3 stark colors, and punchy 8fps stop-motion snaps — unmistakable even from across the room.
new_blurb: Sharp scissor-cut shapes in three flat colors, snapping between poses like stop-motion.
why: 19 words; moved fps into label; blurb now describes the visible effect.

old_blurb: Plots 25 echoing ghost positions behind the moving character with compass bearings and scientific measurement bars.
new_blurb: Leaves 25 fading ghost copies behind the character, plus compass rings and rulers.

new_label: Quiet ink on paper (sumi-e, Japanese brush)
old_blurb: Lots of calm breathing room, crisp folded-paper or brush contours, and deep black sumi ink on pale Shoji paper.
new_blurb: Black brush ink on pale paper with lots of calm empty space.
why: 19 words; "Shoji"/"sumi" unexplained; now plain first, term in parentheses.

old_blurb: Warm glowing amber and gold signals cutting through deep ocean Prussian blue — great for mystery and discovery.
new_blurb: Glowing amber lights cut through deep blue water; feels mysterious and exploratory.
why: 17 words; "Prussian blue" is a pigment name most authors do not know.

old_blurb: Flowing multi-colored trailing ribbons and joyful springy overshoot — celebratory, musical, and full of life.
new_blurb: Colorful ribbons stream behind the hero, who bounces past each mark joyfully.

old_blurb: Shows the visible mechanical joints, pivots, and construction lines of the character like a living Da Vinci notebook.
new_blurb: Shows the character's joints, pivots, and construction lines on a blueprint grid.
why: 18 words; Da Vinci simile replaced with what is actually drawn.

old_blurb: Color fills intentionally shift slightly outside the ink lines like a vintage mid-century silkscreen poster.
new_blurb: Color fills sit slightly off the ink lines, like an old silkscreen poster.

old_blurb: Razor-sharp cut-paper silhouettes with high-contrast color blocks and stepped graphic holds.
new_blurb: Razor-sharp paper silhouettes in three bold colors with stepped, held poses.
why: Near-duplicate of #theme/saul-cutout; recommend merging or renaming to show the difference (mStyle cutout vs saul-severe).

old_blurb: Soft translucent pigment layers bleeding gently into warm textured paper.
new_blurb: Soft see-through paint layers bleed gently into warm textured paper.
why: "translucent pigment" -> plain; near-duplicate of #theme/warm-storybook, flag for merge.

old_blurb: Precision architectural lines, compass rings, and live coordinate readouts on Prussian blue.
new_blurb: Precise drafting lines, compass rings, and live coordinate numbers on navy blue.

old_blurb: Keeps outlines gently shimmering even when the character pauses so the frame never feels frozen or dead.
new_blurb: Outlines keep shimmering during pauses so held poses never look frozen.

old_blurb: A drop of color spreads softly into the paper grain at key emotional moments.
new_blurb: A drop of color spreads softly into the paper at key moments.

old_blurb: Offsets the color shadow 2–3px from the outline so it looks hand-printed rather than computer-perfect.
new_blurb: Nudges the color 2–3 pixels off the outline so it looks hand-printed.

old_blurb: The character pulls back slightly for 3 frames before lunging forward, giving the movement real physical weight.
new_blurb: Character pulls back for three frames before lunging, giving the move weight.

new_label: Bounce past the mark (overshoot and settle)
old_blurb: Instead of stopping robotically, the character goes slightly past its mark and settles back naturally.
new_blurb: Character goes slightly past its target, then settles back naturally.
why: 15 words; leads with the visible effect.

old_blurb: Fins, wings, or ribbons keep moving a split second after the main body stops.
new_blurb: Fins, wings, or ribbons keep moving a moment after the body stops.
why: Label now says what you see; blurb 14 -> 12 words.

old_blurb: Leaves translucent echoes along the path the character just traveled so speed and trajectory are visible.
new_blurb: Leaves fading copies along the path so speed and direction read instantly.

old_blurb: The hero makes a gesture or sound wave, and a companion character enters to answer it in harmony.
new_blurb: Hero sends a signal; a second character enters and answers it.

old_blurb: narrows a circular frame around the key detail so the viewer knows exactly where to look.
new_blurb: Narrows a circle around the key detail so viewers know where to look.

old_blurb: Pauses the action in open space for one beat before the climax so the audience can absorb the story.
new_blurb: Holds the action in open space for one beat so the story sinks in.
why: 19 words; "before the climax" removed because v9 grammar places the breather, not the author.

old_blurb: Strips away interior details so the character reads as a pure, iconic shadow shape.
new_blurb: Strips away inner detail so the character reads as one iconic shape.
why: jargonTerm "Rung 4" leaks into modal; rung numbers are internal.

old_blurb: Expanding rings radiate outward whenever the character turns or strikes a note.
new_blurb: Rings spread outward whenever the character turns or hits a note.

new_label: Hidden shape in the background (figure-ground reversal)
old_blurb: The background shadow carves out the hidden shape of the character without drawing an outline.
new_blurb: The background carves out the character's shape without drawing an outline.

old_blurb: Adds warm organic paper tooth and stippled ink dots so flat shapes feel hand-printed.
new_blurb: Adds paper texture and tiny ink dots so flat shapes feel printed.

old_blurb: Moves the camera closer to the character to heighten intimacy or tension.
new_blurb: Camera creeps closer to the character to build focus or tension.
why: Fine already; tightened to lead with the visible effect.

old_blurb: Tilts the camera angle slightly (-6.5°) when something unexpected or disruptive happens.
new_blurb: Tips the frame slightly when something unexpected or unsettling happens.
why: Degree value moved to label parenthetical.

old_blurb: Glides sideways alongside the character as it travels across the canvas.
new_blurb: Camera glides alongside the character as it crosses the screen.
why: "canvas" is a studio term; "screen" is what the viewer sees.

old_blurb: Adds a brief, energetic camera shudder at the exact moment of climax or impact.
new_blurb: Camera shudders briefly at the exact moment of impact.

old_blurb: Zooms out to reveal the whole landscape and echo the opening frame.
new_blurb: Zooms out to show the whole scene and echo the opening frame.

old_blurb: Locks the camera completely still with wide margins so quiet moments feel sacred.
new_blurb: Camera stops completely, with wide margins, so quiet moments feel sacred.
why: Label now names the role it serves (breather).

old_blurb: Morphs one silhouette directly into the next scene at the exact same screen position.
new_blurb: One shape morphs into the next scene at the same screen spot.

old_blurb: Balanced, organic acceleration and deceleration — the best default for almost any story.
new_blurb: Speeds up and slows down like a real object; the safe default.
why: "acceleration and deceleration" -> plain; jargonTerm cubic-bezier numbers should not show in modal.

old_blurb: Swoops past the destination with theatrical flair before settling into place.
new_blurb: Swoops past the destination with flair, then settles into place.

old_blurb: Steps in bold, rhythmic 8-frames-per-second holds like a cut-paper title sequence.
new_blurb: Steps between poses in bold rhythmic holds, like a cut-paper title sequence.

old_blurb: Slow, steady museum-grade drift across an archival illustration or map.
new_blurb: Drifts slowly and steadily across a still illustration or map.

old_blurb: Holds each pose for 2–3 frames so movement feels sculpted by hand rather than computer-interpolated.
new_blurb: Holds each pose for 2–3 frames so motion feels sculpted by hand.

old_blurb: Graceful arched whale with pleated throat grooves and sweeping pectoral fins.
new_blurb: Graceful arched whale with throat grooves and long sweeping fins.

old_blurb: Sharp geometric falcon with swept primary wings and high-speed diving silhouette.
new_blurb: Sharp geometric falcon with swept wings and a high-speed diving outline.

old_blurb: Diving bell submersible with glowing quartz viewport, sonar dish, and searchlight beam.
new_blurb: Round submersible with a glowing window, sonar dish, and searchlight beam.

old_blurb: Crisp folded paper crane with visible geometric valley-fold creases.
new_blurb: Crisp paper crane with visible fold creases.

old_blurb: Rotating concentric brass rings and 4-point compass rose for navigation and telemetry stories.
new_blurb: Spinning brass rings and a compass rose for navigation and data stories.

old_blurb: Calligraphic fountain-pen nib that draws its own world as it moves.
new_blurb: A pen nib that draws its own world as it moves.

old_blurb: Sculptural acoustic lyre with 5 vibrating strings for musical and synesthetic stories.
new_blurb: Sculpted lyre with five vibrating strings for music and sound stories.

old_blurb: Undulating 5-wave sea-kelp serpent with leafy frond blades and glowing air bulbs.
new_blurb: Wavy kelp serpent with leafy fronds and glowing air bulbs.

new_label: Warm dawn paper (sienna and Prussian blue)
old_blurb: Warm archival paper with Raw Sienna and Prussian blue ink — ideal for handmade openings.
new_blurb: Warm cream paper with rust-brown and deep blue ink; good for openings.
why: "Pelagic", "archival" -> plain; pigment names kept once in label.

new_label: Bold poster trio (ocher and Lyons blue)
old_blurb: Punchy 3-color cut-paper palette with stark Ocher and Lyons Blue contrast.
new_blurb: Three punchy flat colors with stark yellow-brown against blue.
why: Leads with what the colors look like.

old_blurb: Glowing bathyal amber against deep Prussian night for underwater threshold beats.
new_blurb: Glowing amber against deep night-blue water; good for turning points.
why: "threshold beats" is legacy role jargon; v9 calls it the CLAIM/turn.

new_label: Calm paper and ink (shoji and sumi)
old_blurb: High-key Shoji cream with sumi ink wash — ideal for negative-space breather beats.
new_blurb: Pale cream with black ink wash; good for the quiet pause beat.

old_blurb: Cartographic sepia and raw umber for 25-sounding hydrographic trajectory plates.
new_blurb: Map-like sepia and brown for radar trails and survey charts.
why: "25-sounding hydrographic trajectory plates" is pure jargon.

old_blurb: Deep Cotinga violet-blue and warm gold for harmonic duet and finale callbacks.
new_blurb: Deep violet-blue with warm gold; good for duets and finales.
